column2: On the authority of Abū Ḥamzah Anas ibn Mālik (may Allah the Exalted be pleased with him), the servant of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, from the Prophet (Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace), who said: “None of you truly believes until he loves for his brother what he loves for himself.” Reported by al-Bukhārī and Muslim.

Lā yuʾminu (“does not truly believe”): this negation is explained by the narration of Aḥmad with the wording, “A servant does not attain the reality of faith until he loves for people the good that he loves for himself.” This negation often comes to negate some of the obligations of faith while its foundation remains.
“What he loves for himself”: of good, as in the narration of Aḥmad above.
“Good” is a comprehensive word that covers acts of obedience and permissible things, religious and worldly, and excludes what is forbidden.

Among the qualities of faith is that a person loves for his brother what he loves for himself, which entails that he hates for him what he hates for himself. By this the affairs of this world and the Hereafter are set in order,

and people act in accordance with the saying of the Exalted: “And hold firmly to the rope of Allah all together and do not become divided” [Āl ʿImrān 3:103]. Its mainstay and foundation is being free of the diseases of the heart, such as envy and others.
